chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from 'Imran ibn Musa and Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who performs salat (prayer) while in front of him there is an open mushaf in his qiblah, he said: “No.” I said: Then if it is in a cover? He said: “Yes.”

And he said: “A man should not perform salat (prayer) while there is fire or iron in his qiblah.” I said: May he perform salat (prayer) while in front of him there is a brazier of brass? He said: “Yes, but if there is fire in it, then he should not perform salat (prayer) until he moves it away from his qiblah.”

And concerning a man who performs salat (prayer) while in front of him there is a hanging lamp containing fire, except that it is facing him, he said: “If it is raised high, that is worse; he should not perform salat (prayer) facing it.”

key_terms.حَدِيدٌ: iron positioned in the direction of prayer
key_terms.غِلَافٍ: a cover or casing enclosing the mushaf
key_terms.قِنْدِيلٌ: a lamp suspended before the person praying
key_terms.مَفْتُوحٌ: opened, uncovered before the person in salat (prayer)
key_terms.مُصْحَفٌ: a written copy of the Qur'an placed before the worshipper

ai.seo_question: Can a person perform salat (prayer) facing an open mushaf, fire, iron, or a lamp?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about objects placed in front of a person during salat (prayer). It indicates disapproval or impermissibility of praying toward an open mushaf, fire, iron, or a lamp directly facing the worshipper, while permitting certain cases when such objects are covered or removed from the qiblah.
